cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend. Samuel, Israel's prophet, has died, and all Israel mourned him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. Saul, Israel's king, has also removed something from the land.

cards.question: What has Saul removed from the land?

cards.text: Now the Philistines gather and camp at Shunem, and Saul gathers all Israel and camps at Gilboa. Two camps, two armies, and I bet NOBODY is sleeping well tonight.

cards.question: When Saul sees the Philistine army, he feels confident and ready to charge.

cards.text: Saul is afraid and trembles VIOLENTLY. Not a little shiver, friend, the whole-body kind, the kind I did every time somebody yanked open that junk drawer. So Saul inquires of the LORD.

cards.question: Saul is afraid and inquires of the LORD. How does the LORD answer him?

cards.text: No dreams. No Urim. No prophets. So Saul turns to his servants with a request.

cards.question: With no answer from the LORD, Saul tells his servants to find him a woman who is a ___ so he can go and consult her.

cards.text: His servants reply, "There is a medium at Endor." Hold on. Didn't Saul remove the mediums from the land? Somebody missed a spot.

cards.question: Before Saul heads to the medium at Endor, what does he do?

answers.text: He calls for Abiathar the priest

cards.text: In disguise, Saul sets out with two of his men, and they come to the woman at night. Saul says, "Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name."

cards.question: The woman at Endor doesn't know who this stranger is. How does she answer his request?

answers.text: She fears it is a trap to get her killed
She asks to be paid in silver first
She tells him to come back tomorrow

cards.question: Saul answers the woman by swearing to her by the LORD that no punishment will come upon her.

cards.text: Think about that, friend. The man who removed the mediums from the land is now swearing by the LORD to keep one safe.

cards.question: The woman asks whom she should bring up. Saul tells her to bring up ___.
When the woman sees Samuel, she stays calm and quiet.

cards.text: She cries out, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!" The king tells her, "Do not be afraid," and asks what she sees, and she says she sees "a god coming up out of the earth."

cards.question: Saul asks the woman what the figure looks like. What does she describe?

answers.text: An old man wearing a robe
A young man holding a spear
A tall man dressed in armor

cards.question: Once Saul knows it is Samuel, he bows facedown in reverence.

cards.text: Then Samuel speaks to Saul: "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?"
Saul says, "I am deeply distressed." The Philistines are fighting against him, and God has turned away and no longer answers him by prophets or by dreams.

cards.question: Saul has called up Samuel. What does Saul want Samuel to do?

answers.text: Pray to the LORD for him

cards.text: Samuel asks why Saul is consulting him, since the LORD has turned away from Saul and become his enemy. Then Samuel says the LORD has done exactly what He spoke through Samuel.

cards.question: Samuel says the LORD has torn the kingdom out of Saul's hand. Who has the LORD given it to?
Why does Samuel say the LORD has done this to Saul?

answers.text: Saul did not obey the LORD about Amalek
Saul refused to fight the Philistines
Saul took the priests' land for himself

cards.question: Samuel tells Saul that the LORD will deliver Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
Samuel tells Saul that tomorrow Saul and his ___ will be with Samuel.

cards.text: Immediately Saul falls flat on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. And his strength is gone.

cards.question: Saul's strength is gone. What reason does the passage give?

answers.text: He had not eaten all day and night
He had been wounded in battle
He had been sick for many days

cards.text: The woman comes to Saul and sees how distraught he is. She reminds him that she took her life in her hands and did as he told her.

cards.question: Now the woman asks Saul to listen to her. What does she want to do for him?

answers.text: Set some bread before him to eat
Hide him in her house until morning
Bring up Samuel for him once more

cards.question: When the woman offers Saul food, he eats right away.
Saul says, "I will not eat." Who joins the woman in urging him?

cards.text: Saul listens, gets up from the ground and sits on the bed. Getting up after news like that is no small thing, and I say that as a guy who spent YEARS lying in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The woman had a fattened ___ at her house, and she quickly slaughtered it.

cards.text: She also takes flour, kneads it and bakes unleavened bread. Somebody's KNEADING DOUGH in this story? Friend, you know that's the part where I lean in.

cards.question: Saul and his servants eat, and then they stay at her house until morning.

cards.text: Saul and his men walk back out into the night. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is not done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "There is a medium at Endor.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "a god coming up out of the earth.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 2 quotes "I am deeply distressed.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: Saul trembles, the junk-drawer comparison, and Saul inquires of the LORD.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "So Saul inquires of the LORD" presents his fear as the reason he inquires. 1 Samuel 28:6 only says "He inquired of the LORD" and gives no reason.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "the kind I did every time somebody yanked open that junk drawer" adds a new habit to his drawer backstory: trembling violently whenever the drawer opened. The backstory only says they held their breath. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The right answer, "She fears it is a trap to get her killed," states her feeling as fact. In 1 Samuel 28:9 she asks, "Why have you set a trap to get me killed?" The answer should say what she says, for example that she asks why he set a trap to get her killed.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: the woman cries out and recognizes Saul, Saul tells her not to be afraid and asks what she sees, and she answers that she sees a god coming up out of the earth.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card cites only 1 Samuel 28:16. Its second sentence, "the LORD has done exactly what He spoke through Samuel," tells 1 Samuel 28:17. The citation should be 1 Samuel 28:16-17.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Why does Samuel say the LORD has done this to Saul?" uses "this" to point back to the kingdom being torn away, which was on the previous card. That card is no longer on screen. The question should say what "this" is.

rule.text: The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The blank ("fattened ___": calf, lamb or goat) asks the baker to guess an exact word they haven't seen. Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason it out, so getting it right is luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
